dedupe_keys.name: the peering disconnect centralised and virtual peering and the risk to local internet resilience internet society 2026

description: This Internet Society report by Hanna Kreitem examines two shifts in peering that concentrate the Internet: tiered selective peering models, such as Google's Verified Peering Provider model and a Vodafone arrangement with Inter.link, and virtual or remote peering at distant IXPs. It argues they hollow out local infrastructure, entrench monopolies and duopolies, create single points of failure, and add a latency tax of up to about 150 ms to traffic that could stay local, citing the large TIM outages in Italy and the 2022 Rogers outage in which nearly 25% of Canada's Internet connectivity vanished. It concludes that resilience comes from inclusive, physically local and neutral interconnection and refers to a 50/50 vision for local traffic. Producer: Internet Society, 2026. Coverage: global, with examples from Africa, Europe and Canada. Access: free page read in part; the referenced footnotes and any download were not opened. Licence and cost: free; licence not stated. Caveats: an advocacy report with numbers quoted from other sources, and no dataset. Simulation uses: the concentration mechanisms and outage ratios give scenario assumptions for interconnection resilience and capacity models. Related records: the Rogers outage CRTC review (case_study-rogers-outage-2022-crtc-review) and the RIPE Labs IXP incident review (case_study-ripe-labs-why-ixps-matter-critical-infrastructure-ixp-failures).
